html:
The Yavapai are a Native American people of central and western Arizona. They speak a Yuman language, close to that of the Hualapai and the Havasupai. Spanish and American writers often called them "Apache", and the name stuck in the Yavapai-Apache Nation, which unites Yavapai and Tonto Apache families.

They lived in small bands across deserts and mountains, gathering agave, mesquite and acorns, hunting, and farming a little near springs. They traded and fought with the Mojave and the Western Apache.

Gold strikes in the 1860s brought miners and the US Army. In February 1875 about 1,500 Yavapai and Apache were forced to walk from the Verde valley to the San Carlos reservation, and many died on the way. Survivors returned in small numbers from the 1900s. See also Yavapai.
